pr.title: fix(auth): enhance SAML login handling by introducing userId field and updating JWT token structure
pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes SAML IdP-initiated login by correctly setting the JWT `sub` claim to the actual user ID instead of the NameID (email).

### Problem
The SAML IdP provider was using the NameID (configured as email) as the user identifier in the JWT token's `sub` claim. However, the server session explicitly requires `sub` to be the actual user ID, causing session subject mismatches.

### Solution
- Introduces a new `SamlIdpUser` type that includes both `id` (NameID/email) and `userId` (actual user ID)
- Keeps `id` as the NameID to maintain compatibility with BoxyHQ's SAML flow (changing it causes errors)
- Updates the JWT callback to override `sub` with the actual `userId` for the `saml-idp` provider

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [x] I have updated the developer docs in /docs if this PR makes changes that would require a [documentation change](https://cal.com/docs). N/A - no docs changes needed.
- [ ] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.

## How should this be tested?

1. Configure SAML SSO with an IdP (e.g., Okta, Azure AD) with NameID set to email
2. Initiate IdP-initiated login flow
3. Verify that the user session is created correctly with the proper user ID
4. Confirm the JWT token's `sub` claim contains the numeric user ID, not the email

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas

## Human Review Checklist

- [ ] Verify the JWT `sub` override doesn't break other SAML-related functionality
- [ ] Confirm the `SamlIdpUser` type correctly represents all fields returned by the authorize function
- [ ] Test with actual SAML IdP to ensure login flow works end-to-end
